headline: Council gives staff direction on mobile home lot rent ordinance, including a 5% cap on yearly increases.
summary: Under option two from the Housing Committee, lot rents below $520, or 31% of fair market rent for a two-bedroom unit, would not be limited. Councilors also discussed a 34% threshold, which would be $575, and a cap of the lesser of 5% or CPI plus one. Staff will prepare the ordinance for first reading at the November 24 special meeting, with four policy changes from option two. The Charter Commission application deadline is November 24 at 5:30 p.m., and April 13 was discussed as the election date for the Ward 3 seat and the commission.
decisions: Approved consent agenda items one through four, including parking changes and a Crestview Drive deed, 7-0.
Approved the election warrant for a December 15 special mayoral runoff election, 7-0.
Approved suspending council rules and adding a special meeting on November 24, 2026, 5-2.
Approved canceling the December 15, 2026 council meeting because of election day, 6-1.
Approved final passage of curbside trash pickup for owner-occupied mixed-use properties, 7-0.
Continued the public hearing on the mobile home lot rent ordinance to November 24, 7-0.
Approved amendments to the non-union retirement language in personnel policies, 7-0.
Approved lowering the sale price of 55 Old Lisbon Road from $750,000 to $500,000, 7-0.
Approved Councilor Susan Longchamps as the council representative to the loan qualification committee, 7-0.
discussion: Mobile home lot rent ordinance: Councilors discussed exemption thresholds of 28%, 31%, and 34% of fair market rent, plus a 5% cap on yearly increases. Residents asked for lower limits, and other speakers said park operating costs were rising.

Charter Commission: Applications for the three council-appointed seats are due November 24 at 5:30 p.m., and appointments are set for December 1. The city attorney said the nomination period could be shortened from 60 days, and the council discussed holding the election on April 13.

Special meeting and December 15 meeting: The council added a November 24 special meeting and canceled the December 15 meeting because of the runoff election. Public speakers said the special meeting was not needed, and the discussion noted that emergency meetings had been called earlier this year.

Downtown TIF boundary: Economic development staff presented a 342-acre downtown map for a downtown TIF district, with an application expected around March 1. A council member asked for a joint session with the Planning Board before boundaries are set, and the administrator said meeting formats would be discussed.

Maine Resiliency Center survey: The center's director said the survey drew 26 individual participants and 275 respondents. Findings included that recovery is not linear, and a community conversation is set for December 3 at 4:30.
